question.text: Himalaya Growth Partners, a Cat II PE fund, uses the industry benchmark cited in the chapter that private equity firms typically analyze 40-50 investee companies before making one investment. If the fund plans to deploy capital in 8 portfolio companies over its investment period, approximately how many deal screens should the sourcing team plan for?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.1.3.1 (Deal Sourcing for Private Equity Firms), industry practice is 40-50 screens per 1 investment. For 8 investments: 40×8 = 320 to 50×8 = 400 screens. This funnel math drives the size of the sourcing team and scout network. The Trap: 80-100 screens is 10-12 per investment — too thin. 200-300 is 25-35 per investment — still short of the benchmark. 1,000+ overshoots the cited benchmark. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A treats deal sourcing as a concept; XIX-C tests the funnel math directly so the Manager can staff the sourcing team correctly.
